key_concepts: Angiosperms are flowering plants with seeds enclosed within fruits.
Gymnosperms are non-flowering plants with seeds exposed on cones or scales.
Angiosperms often have broad leaves and showy flowers.
Gymnosperms typically have needle-like leaves and cones.
Seeds contain a seed coat, cotyledons, embryo, and sometimes endosperm.
The seed coat is the outer covering of a seed.
The embryo is the undeveloped plant inside a seed.
Endosperm is nutrient storage tissue in seeds.
Angiosperm seeds typically have two cotyledons and may contain endosperm.
Gymnosperm seeds often lack endosperm and have only one cotyledon.
Seeds can be observed and classified by size, shape, color, and texture.
